messages:
IncBot: :rotating_light: [ALERT] Increased 5xx rate for /v1/infer from us-east-1a private subnets (p-subnet-*-a). Error: outbound TCP timeouts to external model hosts. alert_id=net-egress-1754012345
Jordan (oncall): seeing it. paging network oncall. Maya, you available?
Maya (sre): here. looking at graphs. Total p95 latency up, error rate spike ~10:12 UTC. 100% of errors from instances in us-east-1a private subnets.
Jordan (oncall): adding context — deploy bot shows no recent rollout in the region. DeployBot: no deploys in last 2 hours.
Arjun (eng-infra): I'll pull up VPC configs. likely NAT route or route table assoc. grabbing route tables now.
Priya (network): FYI I saw a partial AZ drift in automation earlier — terraform apply failed for AZ A at 09:48 but retried. could be related.
Arjun (eng-infra): running describe-route-tables for the affected subnets:
```
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.subnet-id,Values=subnet-0a1b2c3d

RouteTableId: rtb-0aa11bb22cc
Routes:
  DestinationCidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
  DestinationCidrBlock: 0.0.0.0/0 -> Target: nat-0deadbeef (state: blackhole)
Associations:
  SubnetId: subnet-0a1b2c3d
```
Arjun (eng-infra): route points to nat-0deadbeef which is in "deleting" state -> traffic blackholed. Natgateway shows deleted earlier (maybe during failed terraform).
Maya (sre): that matches the symptom. private instances can reach internal infra but external model hosts time out.
Jordan (oncall): mitigation options? create new NAT in same AZ? route to another NAT in different AZ? fallback to IGW?
Priya (network): we shouldn't route private subnets directly to IGW due to policy and source NAT needs. better to point to a working NAT in another AZ temporarily. security team aware?
Arjun (eng-infra): there is nat-0cafebab in us-east-1b healthy. I can update the route table to point there and re-associate if needed. doing replace-route now (manual).
Arjun (eng-infra): running:
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0aa11bb22cc --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0cafebab
```
Arjun (eng-infra): route replaced. please verify traffic.
Maya (sre): metrics showing immediate drop in 5xx and latency back to normal within 30s. :white_check_mark:
Sam (support): initial customer hits — Support ticket stream shows ~8 customers reported timeouts in us-east-1 between 10:10–10:22 UTC. notifying impacted accounts, sending ETA.
Claire (cs): I sent messages to the affected accounts with summary and that we're mitigating. keeping them updated.
Jordan (oncall): great. marking incident as mitigated. need to decide permanent fix — either recreate NAT in AZ A or update automation to avoid deleting NATs mid-run.
Priya (network): agree. preliminary root cause: terraform drift left route pointing to a deleted NAT (automation applied deletion before route update). will need a harmless change to restore proper NAT per-az.
Arjun (eng-infra): Plan: 1) recreate NAT in AZ A and update route table back (preferred) 2) patch terraform so it does not delete NAT until route re-assoc validated 3) add a guard in CI that prevents destroy if route in use. scheduling a follow-up change.
Maya (sre): I'm taking post-incident follow-up. creating postmortem ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-1428
Jordan (oncall): handing off to Arjun for remediation. I'm going offline for handover in 10. @Arjun please coordinate with Priya for terraform changes.
Arjun (eng-infra): ack. creating fix now. will also run an audit to find any other rtb with blackhole routes.
Arjun (eng-infra): audit snippet:
```
aws ec2 describe-route-tables --query "RouteTables[?Routes[?State=='blackhole']]" --region us-east-1
```
found 1 more rtb in us-east-1c referencing a deleted nat -> opened task.
Sam (support): sent follow-up updates to impacted customers. noted that requests started failing when we had NAT blackhole. customers appreciate quick update.
Priya (network): quick note — we should add an alert for route state changes to catch blackhole routes earlier. filing infra-ops alert request.
Claire (cs): will keep customers informed. adding a short summary for their post-incident email.
Maya (sre): Incident severity downgraded to SEV3 — partial region impact, mitigation in place. Scheduling 30-min postmortem sync at 14:00 UTC. Invites sent.
Jordan (oncall): thanks all. closing incident channel thread once remediation assigned. final note: no data exfil or security impact. only egress failures.
IncBot: Incident incident-1754012345 moved to MITIGATED by Jordan (oncall). duration 00:45:00.
Arjun (eng-infra): created infra change PR to recreate NAT in AZ A and update terraform state: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/pull/587
Maya (sre): adding runbook task: add route-state monitoring and test case for terraform destroy race.
Jordan (oncall): handing final ownership to Arjun for remediation and to Maya for postmortem. thanks everyone. :heart:
